extraction.name: CommonCanvas
extraction.description: A dataset of Creative-Commons-licensed images used to train open diffusion models. The paper pairs curated CC images with synthetic captions to support text-to-image generation.
extraction.creator: Aaron Gokaslan, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, Volodymyr Kuleshov
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors curated a dataset of open-licensed Creative-Commons images and used a pre-trained BLIP-2 model to produce high-quality synthetic captions for the uncaptioned images.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Missing captions were handled by generating synthetic captions with a pre-trained BLIP-2 model.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Synthetic captions were created for caption-less Creative-Commons images using a pre-trained BLIP-2 model; the paper describes this as a transfer-learning-based image-captioning method (“telephoning”).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is biased toward Creative-Commons/open-licensed images and may underrepresent current content; the paper also notes that CommonCanvas under-performs in some categories, like faces.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Known limitations include data incompleteness because most CC images lack captions, data scarcity relative to LAION-2B, and the age of YFCC100M images; the paper also notes that the dataset is not as current as LAION-2B and that future work should augment it with other sources.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work aims to provide a path toward open-licensed text-to-image models that avoid copyright concerns associated with web-scraped training data.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training text-to-image latent diffusion models; the paper also describes it as being used to train and evaluate CommonCanvas models, with commercial and non-commercial subsets.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper states that the dataset and trained model are released, and future plans include augmenting CommonCatalog with Creative-Commons images from other sources and testing larger model architectures; no explicit versioning, maintainer, or deprecation policy is given.

description.evidence: We assemble a dataset of Creative-Commons-licensed (CC) images, which we use to train a set of open diffusion models

rai:dataCollection.evidence: “We suggest a possible path forward, training a suite of T2I architectures using only open-licensed, Creative-Commons (CC) images” and “we use a pre-trained BLIP-2 model ... to produce high-quality, synthetic captions for a set of curated, open licensed CC images.”

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: “we curate CommonCatalog, a dataset of roughly 70 million open-licensed CC images”

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: “almost all CC images lack the captions necessary to train a high-quality T2I model” and “we use a pre-trained BLIP-2 model ... to produce high-quality, synthetic captions”

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: “Curate CommonCatalog, a dataset of roughly 70 million open-licensed CC images”

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: “We address the data incompleteness problem by using a pre-trained BLIP-2 model [34], which we use to produce high-quality, synthetic captions for a set of curated, open licensed CC images.”

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: “we use a pre-trained BLIP-2 model [34], which we use to produce high-quality, synthetic captions”

rai:dataBiases.evidence: “we train on CommonCatalog’s commercial (roughly 70 million) and non-commercial (roughly 25 million) examples” and “Our CommonCanvas models under-perform in some categories, like faces”

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: “The first problem is data incompleteness: almost all CC images lack the captions necessary to train a high-quality T2I model. The second is data scarcity: there are relatively few high-resolution CC images” and “An issue, which we do not address, is that the YFCC100M data is about a decade old; its CC images are not as current as those in LAION-2B.”

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: “Is it possible to efficiently produce a high-quality T2I model by training only on Creative-Commons-licensed data?” and “This reveals a promising path forward for future research on highly-capable, open T2I models.”

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: “we create CommonCanvas, a suite of latent diffusion model (LDM) architectures trained on our curated dataset of CC images and synthetic captions” and “We demonstrate that these models produce competitive qualitative and quantitative results compared to the SD2-base baseline”

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: “Release our CommonCatalog dataset of CC images and synthetic captions along with our trained CommonCanvas model” and “in the future, we plan to augment CommonCatalog with Creative-Commons images from other sources, as well as test larger CommonCanvas model architectures.”
